agent_notes: The signature change is backward-compatible. post(url: string) becomes post(url: string, body?: object), and the new parameter is optional. When body is omitted, `body ?? null` still sends null, exactly as before.

There are 4 existing callers, all URL-only, and I read each one by grep: model-file.service.ts:61, 74 and 87, and server-command.service.ts:26. None of them changes behavior. The only other HttpClient post with null is in auth.interceptor.spec.ts:151, which calls HttpClient directly and is unaffected.

How Angular sends the body: when it is a plain object, HttpClient serializes it as JSON and sets Content-Type: application/json. That matches the backend's switch to bottle.request.json in 111-01, because bottle only parses request.json when that Content-Type is set. A null body sends no Content-Type, so the old no-body POST endpoints behave as before.

A small edge case: the `object` type also accepts FormData, Blob and arrays. FormData or a Blob would change the Content-Type that Angular sends. No current caller passes these, so it is not a defect, just a loose type. A narrower type such as Record<string, unknown> would document the JSON-only intent.

Test coverage: the mock MockRestService (tests/mocks/mock-rest.service.ts) only defines sendRequest, not post. rest.service.spec.ts has no post() tests at all, so the new body pass-through is unverified by unit tests. This belongs to the test-sufficiency lane, but it affects confidence before ConfigService starts depending on it.
Schema/DB impact: none. Performance impact: none (one extra nullish-coalesce per call).

Blast radius of this diff alone is very small. It touches one shared utility method and has no effect on existing callers. The larger risk is outside the diff: phase 111 is half done (backend POST-only, frontend still GET). See imp-001.
Verdict: this diff can ship as-is. Don't deploy HEAD until the frontend ConfigService migration lands.
